title: The Black Friday Bargains Worth Bagging
gist: WIRED's master Black Friday 2026 deals roundup across laptops, Apple, TVs, phones, smart home and more. Beneath the promotional content, recurring signals stand out: broad 2026 consumer-tech price hikes (Roku, Kindle, Kobo, Motorola, Apple, gaming laptops) that make many discounts merely restore old prices, deep TV discounting, and the Mac Mini emerging as a surprise hot product because of local AI.

insights.claim: WIRED reports that Roku, like many consumer tech companies, raised prices significantly across its product lines in 2026, so the Black Friday price of the Roku Streaming Stick Plus only matches its previous regular price; the device once sold for $20.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Industry-wide consumer hardware price hikes mean holiday 'discounts' mask higher ASPs; watch unit volumes versus revenue.
insights.quote: Like many consumer tech companies, Roku raised prices significantly across its product lines.
insights.locator: Here’s the thing: Like many consumer tech companies

insights.claim: Several e-reader and phone makers raised 2026 prices: Amazon hiked the base Kindle price in summer, Kobo raised the Libra Colour from $230 to $260, and Motorola added $100 to the 2026 Moto G Stylus with little to justify it.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Broad-based price increases across low-end devices suggest component or tariff cost pass-through in consumer electronics.
insights.locator: Best Kindle, Tablet, and E-Reader Deals

insights.claim: WIRED says gaming laptops have become so expensive over the past year that it can no longer recommend any option around $1,000, with the Asus ROG Strix G16 RTX 5060 at $1,489 being its cheapest price ever.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: GPU-laptop price inflation may weigh on PC gaming unit demand.
insights.quote: Gaming laptops have gotten really expensive over the past year

insights.claim: Apple's MacBook Air (M5) retail price of $1,299 is described as a bit too expensive, with the $999 Black Friday price making it a must-buy.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Apple's higher list prices make holiday-period demand more promotion-dependent.

insights.claim: WIRED reports the Apple Mac Mini has become a surprise hot product mainly because of surging interest in running AI models locally, working well as an always-on home AI box with at least 32 GB of RAM.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Local AI inference is a new demand driver for Apple desktop hardware and high-RAM configurations.
insights.quote: The Mac Mini has recently become a surprise hot product, primarily thanks to the surge of interest in running AI models locally.

insights.claim: WIRED positions the Mac Studio (M5 Max/M5 Ultra, up to $10,799 for 128 GB) as a machine for creative pros and AI enthusiasts wanting an at-home AI box for coding.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: High-end Apple silicon is being marketed into the local-AI developer segment.

insights.claim: TVs are among the deepest Black Friday 2026 discounts: the 65-inch LG C6 OLED is 48% off at $1,400, TCL QM7L and Hisense U7SG are at all-time lows near $800-$850, and the Roku Pro Series OLED is on sale for the first time.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Aggressive TV price cuts, including on new OLEDs, point to margin pressure in the TV category.
insights.locator: Deals on TVs and Streaming Devices

insights.claim: Samsung's The Frame leads the art-TV category but includes only 30 free art images, requiring a $5 monthly Samsung Art Store subscription for the 5,000-plus catalog, while Amazon's Ember Artline is positioned as a competitor.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Hardware makers are layering subscriptions onto devices; art TVs are a contested niche between Samsung and Amazon.

insights.claim: The Sonos Beam (Gen 2) is at its lowest-ever price of $339, which WIRED attributes likely to the release of the new Sonos Beam Ultra.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Sonos is refreshing its soundbar lineup, clearing older inventory.

insights.claim: Google's Pixel 11 flagships are discounted up to 32%, and WIRED notes Pixels are the only major Android phones with full Qi2 magnetic charging support.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Deep discounts on this year's Pixel flagship suggest Google buying share in premium Android.

insights.claim: Samsung's Galaxy S26 offers seven years of software support and its base model jumped to 256 GB of storage.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Longer support windows may lengthen smartphone replacement cycles.

insights.claim: WIRED's testing found the Samsung Galaxy Watch 9's upgraded chip was not a game changer and its bigger battery did not deliver extra runtime versus the Watch 8.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Incremental smartwatch upgrades weaken the case for annual replacement.
insights.locator: If you don’t need the newest generation, the Samsung Galaxy Watch 8

insights.claim: The repairable, ethically made Fairphone 6, built in Europe, is now available in the US and saw its first discount to $552.
insights.speaker: Simon Hill
insights.so_what: Fairphone's US entry is a small signal for the repairable-device niche.
insights.locator: This is the first discount I’ve seen on the repairable
